benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Choppy: fell almost 9% on 4 Nov after the midterm result, rebounded 3.9% to a $98.29 settlement on 5 Nov (Bloomberg, via Rigzone), then eased slightly to about $98.19 on 6 Nov (Trading Economics), down about 13.5% from a week earlier. Rapidan Energy Group's Bob McNally told CNBC he sees an 80% probability that US-Iran fighting resumes, which he said could push both benchmarks back above $100.

note: Oil and gas whipsawed into 6 November: Brent fell almost 9% on 4 Nov after Democrats won Congress in the midterms, then rebounded 3.9% to $98.29 on 5 Nov (Bloomberg, via Rigzone) as traders weighed a reported Iranian nuclear proposal sent via Qatar against Rapidan Energy Group's Bob McNally, who told CNBC he sees an 80% probability that US-Iran fighting resumes. UKMTO logged a new tanker strike off Qatar's coast on 4 Nov, and Iran's Guards and army made fresh, inconsistent mine claims near the strait on 5 Nov.
